formNote: Mojidata IDS: ⿰土也. The Shuowen explains 地 cosmologically, as what settled when the primal qi divided (see 天 · 地).
summary: The earth, the ground, a place: in correlative cosmology, the heavy and turbid that settled below when the light and clear rose to become Heaven. Its trigram is 坤, the receptive.
placement: At the tip of the lower-left lobe: Earth, one of the Three Powers. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: The Receptive
satellites.evidence: The Shuogua lists each trigram’s images: 乾為天，坤為地 — “Qian is Heaven, Kun is Earth.” The six broken lines of 坤 stand for what receives and bears.
satellites.caveat: A correspondence within the Yijing’s symbolic system, not a claim about the earth.

satellites.title: Earth Among the Four Great Elements
satellites.evidence: In Buddhist translation 地 renders pṛthivī, earth as the first of the four great elements (mahābhūta, 大種). The Abhidharmakośa’s verse: 大種謂四界，即地水火風 — “the great elements are the four realms: earth, water, fire, wind”, each known by its nature, earth’s being hardness (堅).
satellites.caveat: The four great elements are not the five phases (五行), whose earth is 土, not 地. They belong to different systems and answer different questions.

checked.note: 大種謂四界，即地水火風，能成持等業，堅濕煖動性. Checks the Chinese; the Sanskrit is not checked here.
